clue.text: One gives a sleeper a ring in the ear

definitions.text: One gives a sleeper a ring in the ear

parts.words: One gives a sleeper a ring in the ear
parts.note: reads like someone phoning a sleeping friend, but the ring is the bell of a bedside device that wakes you

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a dozing friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedside timepiece rings loudly at a set hour to wake whoever is asleep.

clue.text: A rising multitude in a state in India

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards, so it runs backwards

parts.note: a mass is a multitude, a great crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd swells in one of India's regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns MASS into SSAM, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a north-eastern Indian state, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Really knocked out, suck water freely

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters move about without constraint, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down water without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges the nine letters of SUCK WATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being filled with awe is being deeply impressed, informally knocked out.

clue.text: Suspect acts to put 500 on dealings…

parts.note: in British slang a monkey is five hundred pounds
business is commercial dealings

explanation.surface: Someone stakes 500 on shady trades, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY is British slang for £500. 'to put ... on' just places the pieces side by side, MONKEY first in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief or underhand behaviour is a set of dubious acts, as in 'no funny stuff'.

clue.text: … some companies may be cramped by one

definitions.text: some companies may be cramped by one

parts.words: some companies may be cramped by one
parts.note: companies called Ltd are limited, so something that restricts or restrains them is what cramps them

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: some firms are hemmed in by a regulator.
explanation.definitionFit: A device or person that restricts something sets limits, as limited companies have limited liability.

clue.text: May one, in Rome? Not these days!

definitions.text: May one, in Rome? Not these days!

parts.words: May one, in Rome? Not these days!
parts.note: the first day of May in the Roman calendar had a special name, a dating system no longer used today

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission in Rome and is told it is no longer done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May one' looks like a polite question; it is the first of May. The Romans called the first day of each month by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar the first day of every month bore this name, so 1 May fell on it.

clue.text: States points and functions

parts.note: US is the United States
E (east) is a compass point
S (south) is a compass point

explanation.surface: A list of a country's assertions and purposes.
explanation.definitionFit: Purposes or roles something serves are its applications.

clue.text: Celebrity embracing one is a step up

indicators.note: embracing means the first word holds the second inside it, as arms hug

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A famous person hugging someone is a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step in a flight leading up between floors.

clue.text: Border poet showing whiskers

parts.note: a side is an edge or border
Robert Burns is the Scottish poet

explanation.surface: A poet from the Scottish Borders displays a beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Border' hints at the Scottish Borders region, but it simply gives SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair grown down the side of the face in front of the ears.

clue.text: Being secret in planning to serve cola in airports

indicators.note: planning suggests the letters are being arranged anew, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discreet arrangements to sell soft drinks in airport terminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planning' rearranges COLA IN AIRPORTS; 'to serve' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Conspirators share hidden plots, so the adjective describes a hushed, plotting manner.

clue.text: Flat bone from Munster workings

indicators.note: workings suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A bone dug up in the Irish province of Munster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workings' rearranges MUNSTER. Munster is a province of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the long flat bone in the middle of the chest.

clue.text: Close-fitting garment for Sylvia, for example

definitions.text: Close-fitting garment for Sylvia, for example

parts.words: Close-fitting garment for Sylvia, for example
parts.note: Sylvia is a ballet by Delibes, so this is the tight garment worn by its dancers

explanation.surface: A tight dress for a woman named Sylvia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sylvia' looks like a woman's name; it is the title of a ballet, so the garment is a dancer's.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece skin-tight costume worn by ballet dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Decrepit, he meant to change

indicators.note: to change signals the letters of the words are altered in order

explanation.surface: He intended to reform his tumbledown ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth chewed full of holes by insects looks worn out and shabby.

clue.text: After science, wipe and clean up

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first in the answer

parts.note: Sc is a standard abbreviation for science
to rub is to wipe

explanation.surface: Following a lab session, someone cleans the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour hard with a brush is to wash thoroughly.

clue.text: Small general digit?

explanation.surface: A short army officer counts on his fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of a famously tiny 19th-century showman.
explanation.definitionFit: General Tom Thumb was a tiny showman's title; the short thick first finger of the hand is the other sense.

clue.text: Telegraphed response heard from Terpsichorean

indicators.note: heard means the words are said aloud and the sound gives the entry

parts.note: a reply sent by telegraph is a tapped answer, keyed out in Morse

explanation.surface: A Morse reply comes from a devotee of dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'tapped answer' sounds like the entry. Terpsichore is the Greek muse of dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Terpsichorean means relating to dance, here a dancer, one who clicks steel-tipped shoes.

clue.text: He cancelled chores Cinderella included

indicators.note: included shows the entry sits within the run of the neighbouring words

explanation.surface: A man let Cinderella off her housework.
explanation.definitionFit: One who revokes or annuls something is the person who called it off.

clue.text: Shame, dragging engineers into quarrel

indicators.note: dragging into means one piece is pulled inside the other

parts.note: a dispute is a quarrel
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: It is embarrassing to pull engineers into a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dragging ... into' puts RE (Royal Engineers) inside DISPUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of good reputation means disgrace.

clue.text: Fish-pole as plain weapon

parts.note: the pike is a freshwater fish
a staff is a pole

explanation.surface: An angler's rod used as a basic arm.
explanation.walkthrough: The plain shaft of a pike was proverbial: 'as plain as a pikestaff'.
explanation.definitionFit: The wooden shaft of an old infantry spear, proverbial for being obvious.

clue.text: Lack producing cardiac

parts.note: recalls the proverb that being away makes the heart grow fonder, so a lack has an effect on the heart

explanation.surface: A deficiency causing heart trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardiac' means of the heart, nodding to the proverb 'makes the heart grow fonder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away or the want of something is a lack, which the proverb says warms the heart.

clue.text: Iron men and women

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
males are men

explanation.surface: Ironmongers, men and women all listed together.
explanation.definitionFit: The sex that bears young; women collectively.

clue.text: Domed recess as an afterthought, is added

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, A
PS (postscript) is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: An alcove with a dome was tacked on later.
explanation.definitionFit: Another word for an apse, the vaulted semicircular end of a church.

clue.text: Gas or gibberish that does not begin

indicators.note: something that does not begin has lost its opening, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: jargon is unintelligible talk, gibberish

explanation.surface: Either hot air or nonsense that never gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that does not begin' drops J from JARGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas, an inert element found in air.

clue.text: Field condition making progress

explanation.surface: A pitch is fit for play and things are advancing.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing term for the state of the turf, and also advancing.

clue.text: Lemons, not treated, dropping off

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: Untreated citrus fruit falling from the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges LEMONS NOT; 'not' reads as part of 'not treated' but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy, about to fall asleep.

clue.text: Lifting the shorter foot

parts.note: ft is the short form of foot

explanation.surface: Raising the smaller foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' looks like raising a foot; it is slang for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for stealing.

clue.text: Cycle colour borders on deep red

parts.note: c is the standard abbreviation for cycle
rims are edges or borders

explanation.surface: A bicycle's paint is tinged with a dark scarlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, strong shade of scarlet.

clue.text: Attraction around English island in holiday time

indicators.note: around means the first word wraps round the others

parts.note: a lure is an attraction

explanation.surface: An English island resort draws holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Free time away from work, when one is on vacation.

clue.text: See red when gear-changing

indicators.note: changing means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A driver loses temper while shifting gears.
explanation.definitionFit: To be furious is to be angry, to see red.

clue.text: The most savage basset I let loose

indicators.note: let loose suggests the letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Releasing a basset hound, the fiercest dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of beastly: most brutal and cruel.
